join.outside_window_note: These rows precede or follow the P1 registered-callback observation window; they are not classified as failed callbacks.

interpretation.interrupt_callback_correlation: All 932 P1 nested callback observations map in order, one-to-one, to distinct continuous P2 PM4_INTERRUPT IDs 965..1896. The matched rows all use source=1, CPU mask/dispatched mask 0x04, CPU2, wrapper 0x823B37B8, and data 0xB7365F00.
interpretation.record_reuse: P1 observed callback data 0xC9684880 568 times and 0xC969D480 once; those calls map to distinct PM4 interrupt IDs. This demonstrates repeated use of a guest record address, not an accidental duplicate interrupt. Repeated packet-source/ordinal pairs show command-buffer locations are reused, so the trace does not prove each dispatch represents a semantically new GPU completion.
interpretation.completion_marker: The 189 calls through stream 0xC969137C each attach to a distinct dequeue ticket and each observe token 0xC0000000; 188 share words [0xC0000000,0x22080,0,0], one has [0xC0000000,0,0x41D40000,0]. This proves distinct handler invocations over distinct queue tickets, but not whether the token marks a fresh completion or stale state revisited for each ticket.
interpretation.counter_underflow: The captured counter has two +1 stores and 189 -1 stores, ending at signed -187. The decrement path is guest worker code; PM4 dispatch counts alone do not establish that these decrements are erroneous.
limits: P1 records nested registered callback targets; P2 records the outer callback wrapper and data passed to ExecuteInterrupt. Timestamp/order correlation does not prove payload equivalence or guest semantic completion.
The capture did not confirm the main menu and does not establish retail renderer parity.
